![Khao Man Gai Tod Recipe (Thai Fried Chicken Rice) | Saveur](https://api.dataforseo.com/cdn/i/07280527-1672-0139-0000-24f21b9e9a8d:6)
**Khao man gai tod** (ข้าวมันไก่ทอด) is the beloved `crispy fried chicken variant of Thailand’s iconic Hainanese chicken rice` . It features seasoned, golden-fried chicken served over jasmine rice cooked in rich chicken broth and fat, alongside sliced cucumbers, a side of warm chicken soup, and *nam jim gai* (sweet chili sauce).[](https://www.saveur.com/recipes/khao-man-gai-tod-fried-chicken-rice/) [[1]](https://www.saveur.com/recipes/khao-man-gai-tod-fried-chicken-rice/)[[2]](https://hot-thai-kitchen.com/hainanese-chicken-rice/)[[3]](https://www.facebook.com/richardbarrowthailand/posts/chicken-on-rice-khao-man-gai-%E0%B8%82%E0%B9%89%E0%B8%B2%E0%B8%A7%E0%B8%A1%E0%B8%B1%E0%B8%99%E0%B9%84%E0%B8%81%E0%B9%88-is-one-of-those-meals-you-can-eat-any-ti/1560739035412354/)

Key Components

- **The Rice:** Unmolded into a perfect dome, the jasmine rice gets its rich flavor and signature glossy sheen from being sautéed in rendered chicken fat and cooked in a fragrant chicken stock.
- **The Chicken:** Usually made with boneless thighs. The secret to the legendary street-food crunch is the batter, which typically combines plain flour, rice flour, cornflour, and a pinch of baking soda for a light, crispy, and airy coating.[](https://www.marionskitchen.com/thai-fried-chicken-rice-khao-mun-gai-tod/) [[1]](https://www.marionskitchen.com/thai-fried-chicken-rice-khao-mun-gai-tod/)[[2]](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DHu2mJyTXpl/?hl=en)
- **The Sauce:** Unlike the ginger-soy dip served with boiled *khao man gai* , the fried version is classically paired with a sweet chili sauce specifically made for chicken, offering a bright, sweet, and slightly tangy flavor profile.[](https://www.saveur.com/recipes/khao-man-gai-tod-fried-chicken-rice/) 

How to Order in Thailand When visiting street food stalls or food courts in Thailand, you can order a straight plate of fried chicken rice by asking for "khao man gai tod". If you can't decide between the classic boiled chicken (*kai tom* ) and the fried version (*tod* ), you can ask for a mixed plate by ordering "khao man gai luam".[](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/mLNs2iap8Ow) [[1]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/mLNs2iap8Ow)For a quick, foolproof recipe on how to master the perfect crispy batter and aromatic rice at home:![Related video thumbnail](https://encrypted-tbn2.gstatic.com/images?q=tbn:ANd9GcQE5l8FUQjWtN8eKim4-oZKYeoPh5BcY9fBzplWdXvr1aQ7BFN0)
